Dynamic Programming|Easy|Dynamic Program.question: What is dynamic programming?
options: A method to solve complex problems by breaking them into simpler subproblems.

Greedy Algorithm|Easy|Greedy Algorithm.question: What is a greedy algorithm?
options: An algorithm that makes the best immediate choice at each step.

Week 3|Easy|Big-O Notation.question: Assume that a computer can execute 10^8 operations in 1 second. If the time limit is 1 to 2 second and input size is 10^8, what is the max acceptable time complexity?
options: O(n)

Week 3|Easy|Time complexity for Array.question: What is the time complexity of 1) indexing into an array, 2) appending an element to an array? If one of them is not possible, explain why.
options: 1) indexing into an array takes O(1) time. 2) appending to array is not possible, because arrays are statically allocated. Array's length is initialized at the start.

Week 3|Easy|Time complexity for Dynamic.question: What is the time complexity of adding or removing elements in the middle of a Dynamic Array/List? Why?
options: O(n), becasue of the need to shuffle/move up all the subsequent elements.

Week 3|Easy|Time complexity for Sorting.question: What is the time complexity of sorting an array? What is one sorting algorithm that meets this time complexity?
options: O(n log n). Merge sort, quick sort, etc.

Week 4|Easy|Array vs List Access.question: Compare time complexities for accessing elements in arrays and lists.
options: Arrays and lists: O(1) for access. Lists: O(n) for insert at specific index.

Week 4|Medium|Sliding Window Technique.question: What is the Sliding Window technique and when is it used?
options: Sliding Window is used for subarray problems. It maintains a window over the data and usually runs in O(n) time.

Week 4|Medium|Two Pointers Technique.question: Explain the Two Pointers technique and its typical time complexity.
options: Two Pointers is used with sorted arrays to iterate from both ends towards the center. It typically runs in O(n) time.

Week 5|Easy|Python Sorting Complexity.question: What is the time complexity of Python's built-in sorting function?
options: Python's built-in sorting function has a time complexity of O(n log n).

Week 5|Medium|Binary Search.question: What is binary search and its time complexity?
options: Binary search finds an element in a sorted array by repeatedly halving the search space. Its time complexity is O(log n).

Week 5|Medium|Hash Tables.question: What are hash tables and their average time complexities?
options: Hash tables allow O(1) average time for insert, delete, and lookup of key-value pairs.

Week 5|Medium|Merge Sort.question: Briefly explain merge sort and its time complexity.
options: Merge sort recursively splits the array into halves and merges them back. Its time complexity is O(n log n).

Week 6|Easy|Singly Linked List.question: Describe the structure and time complexity of operations in a singly linked list.
options: A chain of nodes where each points to the next. Accessing nth element is O(n), adding after nth is O(1).

Week 6|Easy|Stacks and Queues.question: How are stacks and queues implemented in Python and what are their main operations?
options: Stacks use lists (pop(), append()), queues use deque. Both provide O(1) access to top elements.

Week 6|Medium|Linked List Operations.question: What are the time complexities for main operations in a linked list?
options: Insertion and deletion at known position: O(1). Search: O(n).

Week 7|Hard|BST vs Balanced BST.question: Compare time complexities of operations in a BST vs a balanced BST.
options: Regular BST: O(n) worst case. Balanced BST: O(log n) for search, insert, delete.

Week 7|Medium|Binary Search Tree.question: What is a binary search tree (BST) and its main advantage?
options: A tree where left subtree < node < right subtree. Allows O(log n) search

Week 7|Medium|DFS Time Complexity.question: What is the time complexity of depth-first search (DFS) in a tree?
options: The time complexity of DFS in a tree is O(n) where n is the number of nodes.

Week 7|Medium|DFS vs BFS.question: Compare DFS and BFS traversal methods and their use cases.
options: DFS uses stack, good for deep trees. BFS uses queue, good for shortest path.

Week 8|Hard|Heaps.question: What are heaps and their time complexities for main operations?
options: Heaps are priority queues. Insert and remove: O(log n). Access min/max: O(1).

Week 9|Hard|Heap Operations.question: What are the time complexities of main heap operations?
options: Insert: O(log n). Delete min/max: O(log n). Access min/max: O(1). Heapify: O(n).
